topic.title: Learning-Guided Combinatorial Search
topic.overview: Combinatorial problems require choosing discrete structures from an enormous candidate space. These papers use learned policies, continuous proposal spaces, meta-learning, and memory to guide search for routing and other optimization tasks. The dominant theme is learning where to search or how to adapt a solver, rather than replacing feasibility constraints with an unconstrained prediction.
topic.whyItMatters: A neural solver that works only on its training distribution may fail when instance size or structure changes. Combining learned proposals with adaptable selection and explicit search can improve both scalability and robustness.
topic.evolution: Early representatives compare soft assignment and genetic-search strategies, followed by learning to guide branch-and-bound. Recent work learns distributions of candidate solutions, adapts policies in latent spaces, and selects among solvers. The 2026 evidence distinguishes proposing promising actions from committing to one, motivating more transferable proposal-and-selection designs.
openQuestions: Which learned search components generalize across problem families and scales?
How can solution-quality guarantees be retained during rapid online adaptation?
